unknowns: Target concentration ranges for glucose and lactate.
Required accuracy, detection limit and response time.
Reference method details: analyzer type, sampling frequency and its own uncertainty and delay.
Matrix composition: medium components, feed additions, dissolved gas, pH and their variation during the run.
Cell population: suspended or adherent cells, cell density and viability, and resulting light scattering.
Optical behaviour of the medium: clear, turbid or scattering, and how it changes during the run.
Whether the measurement is inside the bioreactor (in situ) or in a sidestream, and the installation point and optical path length.
Temperature, pressure and sterilisation requirements (e.g. autoclaving, CIP/SIP) at the measurement point.
Fouling and cleaning: deposit formation on the optical interface and cleaning regime.
Calibration strategy and model maintenance over a changing medium and cell population.
Measurement modality and probe type (e.g. NIR, Raman, MIR) and whether a fluorescent indicator is intended.
Number and timing of pilot runs available for comparison with the laboratory measurements.
